1004868.etyen:
From Fransk (“French”) + Guinea (“Guinea”), literally “French Guinea”. The name corresponds to French Guinée française (“French Guinea”).
Parallel formations include Norwegian Nynorsk Fransk Guinea, Swedish Franska Guinea, Danish Fransk Guinea, Finnish Ranskan Guinea and English French Guinea.

1005124.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂éd
Compound of ciss-moll (“C-sharp minor”) + akkord (“chord”), literally “C-sharp-minor chord”.
The first element ciss-moll (“C-sharp minor”) contains ciss (“C-sharp”), formed from c (“C”) and -iss (“sharp-note-forming suffix”); the suffix is from German -is (“sharp-note-forming suffix”), whose further origin is uncertain. The second part of ciss-moll, moll (“minor”), is via German Moll (“minor”) from Middle High German bēmolle (“B-flat; soft B”), from Medieval Latin b molle (“soft B”).
